questions.prompt: A regulator requires that customer data never leave India. Which concept decides where the data lives?
questions.explanation: Data residency is a Region choice. AZs are inside a Region; edge locations only cache; the account is a global container.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum number of Availability Zones a production workload should span?

options.text: As many as the Region has

questions.explanation: Two is the rule; three is common for quorum-based systems, but two already survives a single-AZ failure.

questions.prompt: Which of these services operate from edge locations? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: CloudFront and Route 53 answer from the edge. RDS and EC2 run inside a Region's AZs.

questions.prompt: The AZ named ap-south-1a always refers to the same physical site in every AWS account.
questions.explanation: AZ names are mapped per account. Use the AZ ID (e.g. aps1-az1) to coordinate across accounts.

questions.prompt: Why do organisations run separate AWS accounts for dev and prod?

options.text: Because a Region can only hold one environment
To limit the blast radius of mistakes and to separate billing and permissions
Because IAM does not work across Availability Zones

questions.explanation: An account is the top-level boundary for identity, billing and blast radius.

questions.prompt: Users in Mumbai see slow page loads from an application running in us-east-1. The static assets are already on CloudFront. What most directly reduces latency for the dynamic API calls?

options.text: Add a second Availability Zone in us-east-1
Create a new AWS account in India

questions.explanation: Latency to a Region is fixed by geography. Extra AZs help availability, not distance; accounts are not geographic; edge locations do not run the API.
